blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Rollout loop sizing matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Agent RL throughput is set by the rollout loop, not the gradient step, so the serial slot cycle caps capacity and Amdahl's law bounds any single-stage speedup.

questions.q: The section **Exercises** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: GRPO replaces the learned critic with G rollouts per task and broadcasts one standardized coefficient to every sampled token of a rollout, and its clipping and KL estimator choices change how that signal is weighted.
Ratios and gradients are valid only on per-invocation records of the delivered prefix token IDs, sampled token IDs, and behavior log probabilities under the actual sampling transforms.
Agent RL throughput is set by the rollout loop, not the gradient step, so the serial slot cycle caps capacity and Amdahl's law bounds any single-stage speedup.
Once a check is the objective, any trajectory with proxy reward at least the intended solution's but lower true utility gains weight, and cheap exploits usually have high probability.
